On Palm Sunday, 21 March 1937, police in Ponce, Puerto Rico, opened fire on a peaceful march of the Nationalist Party. Nineteen people were killed, among them bystanders, and some two hundred were wounded.

The march marked the end of slavery in 1873 and protested the jailing of Pedro Albizu Campos. The US-appointed governor, Blanton Winship, had the permit revoked at the last minute, and police surrounded the marchers.

A commission led by the American Civil Liberties Union called it a massacre and blamed the governor. No one was punished. The killings deepened nationalist anger toward US rule, which had come with the invasion of 1898.
sum: On Palm Sunday, 21 March 1937, police in Ponce, Puerto Rico, opened fire on a peaceful march of the Nationalist Party. Nineteen people were killed, among them bystanders, and some two hundred were wounded.
